name: Laundry detergent boosters/additives
anchor: data/taxonomy/hmtc-v2.json categories[] n=19, thirteen subcategory slugs; exposure pathway 'Dermal (residue on fabric in prolonged skin contact)'. The taxonomy's regulatory_anchors field names Green Seal GS-48 scope and EPA Safer Choice laundry product types; those are SCOPING anchors that define what belongs in the category, not sources of numeric limits, and neither sets a heavy-metal maximum level.
native_basis_label: total heavy-metal content of the finished product as placed on the market (as-sold consumer-chemical product-content basis, mg/kg of product). Basis limitation, stated because this row spans more than one concentration format: this is a product-content ceiling on the product AS SOLD and it is not dose-equivalent across ready-to-use, concentrated, super-concentrated and unit-dose formats. No reconstitution, dilution or per-wash dose conversion is applied, because no sovereign instrument writes one for this product class and Method v2.0 forbids inventing one; the single reconstitution conversion in the programme, 8:1, is confined to infant formula. The consequence is disclosed rather than hidden: a super-concentrated unit-dose format and a dilute ready-to-use format that both sit at the ceiling deliver different metal loads per wash, so the ceiling must not be read as an equal-exposure statement between formats. Anti-circumvention: a reformulation that lowers the as-sold concentration without lowering the metal load delivered per dose is recorded as a non-improvement, does not satisfy ALARA and does not move the product within the control band, and the declared dose and per-dose metal load are recorded on every lot record so that the comparison can be made
scope_note: Mined and refined mineral concentrates — sodium borate, sodium carbonate (soda ash), sodium sulfate, sodium percarbonate, and zeolite or phosphate water softeners — together with enzyme, surfactant and chelant boosters. The product is dosed into wash water alongside a detergent and rinsed; the dermal pathway is residual carryover on fabric worn in prolonged skin contact, plus the wash-water discharge pathway. This row is the most mineral-intensive in the category: borate, soda ash, sulfate and percarbonate are mined or mineral-derived feedstocks, and geogenic lead, cadmium and arsenic carried through from the ore body is the dominant contamination pathway rather than process contact. Boundary rules for this category: the product must be intended to contact fabrics during washing, drying or treatment; a carpet cleaner is Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) unless it is specifically a fabric-care product for upholstery; and dryer sheets route to the fabric-softener row. No sovereign contaminant maximum exists for this product form. The four toxic-panel cells and the nickel cell are disclosed read-across values from the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical maximum levels in this row's native basis; the remaining unregulated cells are held under mandatory analytical control with a published method and escalation rule; and the two speciation cells are bounded by their total-element parents. No cell is occurrence-derived.
basis_guard: cosmetic product|finished cosmetic as sold|marketed cosmetic product|cosmetic colourant impurity
basis_guard_note: Every numeric cell on this row is a disclosed read-across from a sovereign maximum level set on a FINISHED CONSUMER-CHEMICAL PRODUCT expressed as total content of the product as placed on the market. The guard admits only that basis family (80 of the register's 2,993 rows as built) and therefore blocks, at compile time, the four basis conflations that would otherwise be available and would each be indefensible: a dietary wet-weight or as-consumed food maximum level; the EU consumer-textile restriction, which is a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis on the FABRIC rather than a content basis on the product applied to it; article migration and soluble-migration limits (EU Directive 2009/48/EC toys, jewellery and school-article rules); and percent-by-weight deliberate-use article restrictions (EU REACH Annex XVII entries 20, 23 and 47, EU RoHS, and the tattoo and permanent-make-up mixture basis of entry 75). Those instruments are named and dispositioned in the cell substantiations and, where they govern a genuinely related form, are carried as companion limits on the control cells; none of them can anchor a number here.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; no sovereign sets a contaminant maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, so each toxic-panel cell is a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical maximum level in the product's native as-sold content basis, and each remaining unregulated cell is a control with a published method and escalation rule; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.basis: total lead content of the product as placed on the market (consumer-chemical product-content basis; disclosed read-across)
Pb.source_scope: cosmetic products in general except listed higher-lead make-up categories
Pb.label: disclosed read-across from the German BVL 2017 orientation value for this analyte in a finished cosmetic product, the strictest coherent sovereign consumer-chemical regime applicable to a fabric-care product in this row's native as-sold product-content basis
Pb.substantiation: Program-wide consistency ruling (2026-08-17): the German BVL 2017 orientation values are treated as SELECTABLE anchors across HMTc. The live Category 15 standard tags three of these same register rows regulatory-alignment, and Categories 2, 13, 14 and 20 bind them directly, so the earlier Category 19 position that a register status of 'guidance impurity limit' makes them unselectable contradicted five sibling categories on the identical rows, and did so in the looser direction (5x on lead, 50x on cadmium, 4x on total arsenic, 10x on total mercury). BVL is a single coherent sovereign consumer-chemical regime covering all four toxics, so reading it across preserves this category's own rule of adopting one coherent regime per analyte rather than picking the lowest number across regimes. The China NMPA 2015 value previously published is retained as a named looser comparator. Whether a national enforcement orientation value ranks as a sovereign maximum level is a genuine governance question, recorded for ratification as OI-20260817-bvl-selectability-ruling; until it is ruled on, every category states the same rule. Previously bound: cn_nmpa2015_pb_cosmetics_10.

Ni.basis: total nickel content of the product as placed on the market (consumer-chemical product-content basis; disclosed read-across)
Ni.source_scope: cosmetic products other than eye makeup or color makeup products
Ni.label: disclosed read-across from Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 cosmetics safety standards (carried forward unchanged from Notice 2024-9) (10 mg/kg nickel in a finished consumer-chemical product other than eye or colour make-up), the nearest applicable sovereign maximum level on a finished consumer-chemical product in this row's native basis
Ni.substantiation: Nickel is the analyte this category's exposure pathway is built around: nickel is a confirmed dermal sensitiser, and a residue deposited on fabric that is then worn is prolonged, repeated dermal contact. No sovereign sets a nickel maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. China NMPA 2015 Table 2 — the instrument that anchors lead, cadmium, arsenic and mercury on this row — sets no nickel limit at all, so for nickel the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical value is the Korean statutory limit, which is the only regime in the register that sets one. The Korean instrument writes a product-form split (eye make-up 35, colour make-up 30, all other cosmetic products 10 mg/kg); the split is preserved and the "all other products" tier is the applicable one, because a fabric-care product is not a decorative make-up. A single coherent sovereign regime is read across per analyte rather than the lowest number picked across regimes, which would build a ceiling no sovereign enforces. China NMPA 2015 Table 2 is the strictest coherent STATUTORY consumer-chemical regime for lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury (Korea MFDS is looser on lead at 20 and on total arsenic at 10 mg/kg; the ASEAN, Health Canada and Germany BVL values are cosmetics-scoped administrative or technical-avoidability findings rather than statutory maximum levels, and are on-scope-only under governance ruling GR-2026-08-17-BVL), and the same instrument is already the published read-across anchor of the live Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) standard for the identical logical move, verified 2026-08-17 against the live page https://heavymetalcertified.com/standards/all-purpose-cleaners (Category 12 standard version 1.0, dated 2026-08-13), which publishes lead 10, cadmium 5, total arsenic 2 and total mercury 1 mg/kg with provenance read-across and binding source China Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics (2015, NMPA), the values carried by register rows cn_nmpa2015_pb_cosmetics_10, cn_nmpa2015_cd_cosmetics_5, cn_nmpa2015_tas_cosmetics_2 and cn_nmpa2015_thg_cosmetics_1, and which states the same single-coherent-regime rule; the Category 12 records were rendered by a dedicated certification-repository builder rather than through this repository's compiled-standards manifest, so the live page and not an in-repo artifact is the citation a reader checks. Nickel is not regulated by the Chinese instrument at all, so for nickel the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical value is the Korean statutory limit; that is the only regime in the register that sets one, and no number in this row was chosen by comparing outcomes. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 27 restricts nickel RELEASE from articles in prolonged skin contact rather than nickel content in a mixture and is not carried in the register as a content limit, so it is not read across; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 sets no nickel row for consumer textiles, so no downstream fabric content ceiling is available for this analyte. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 (Regulation (EU) 2020/2081) sets the strictest sovereign consumer-mixture metal limits in the register (lead 0.7, cadmium 0.5, total arsenic 0.5, mercury 0.5, Cr(VI) 0.5 and nickel 5 mg/kg), but its scope is mixtures for tattooing and permanent make-up, an intradermal-injection route. Reading an injected-mixture ceiling across to a rinse-off or fabric-deposited topical product would conflate exposure routes, and its register basis is a tattoo/permanent-make-up mixture basis that this row's basis_guard excludes. Nickel is measured in soaps, detergents and household hygienic products in the routed corpus and is named for laundry care by greenseal2020-gs51-laundry-care-products, nydec2020-cleansing-product-disclosure-bmp and ecetoc1992-tr045-ni-co-cr-consumer-products, so a not-material determination is unavailable on the facts. Complete disposition of the stricter rows the compiler's audit safety-net surfaces for this row, none of which is adopted. (1) de_bvl2017_pb_cosmetics_general_2000 (2 mg/kg), de_bvl2017_cd_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1), de_bvl2017_tas_cosmetics_general_500 (0.5) and de_bvl2017_thg_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1): Germany BVL 2017 technical-avoidability findings for cosmetic manufacture, register status 'guidance impurity limit', dispositioned under HMTc governance ruling GR-2026-08-17-BVL as on-scope-only and therefore unavailable as a read-across anchor for a non-cosmetic product class. The ruling is stated in full in this configuration's credible_note and is the single programme-wide rule the live Category 15 (Feminine Care) standard and this category both now state; Category 15 binds these same four BVL rows because its rows ARE cosmetics, and every number Category 15 publishes is unaffected by the ruling. (2) hc_cosmetic_cd_3ppm (3 mg/kg): a Health Canada cosmetic impurity guidance limit, excluded for the same reason, and adopting it for cadmium alone would additionally mix regimes. (3) eu_2018_1513_pb_consumer_textiles_1mgkg, eu_2018_1513_cd_consumer_textiles_1mgkg and eu_2018_1513_tas_consumer_textiles_1mgkg (1 mg/kg each): the EU consumer-textile restriction, which governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than this row's product-content basis; carried as a downstream constraint and companion limit, and blocked from anchoring by the row's basis_guard. The audit_exclude_scope on this row removes only the oral/mucosal toothpaste tier, tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures, and colour-additive and colourant specifications; against the register as built it suppresses no row that the audit scope would otherwise surface, so nothing was excluded to make this list shorter. (4) Two further stricter rows exist that the compiler's audit safety-net structurally CANNOT surface, because it filters to the credible-regulator set, and they are therefore recorded by hand rather than left invisible. asean2019_th_cd_cosmetic_products_3000 (Thailand, cadmium 3 mg/kg) is a guidance impurity limit and falls to the same reasoning as the Health Canada value. eaeu_trcu009_2011_pb_natural_raw_material_cosmetics_5mgkg (EAEU, lead 5 mg/kg) is the only STATUTORY row anywhere in the consumer-chemical product-content basis family that is stricter than an anchor adopted here, and it is not adopted for three reasons: the EAEU is not in the HMTc credible-regulator set and admitting it is a governance ruling outside this derivation; its scope is formulation-conditioned (perfumery-cosmetic products containing more than 1 per cent natural plant or natural mineral raw material) rather than the general product tier, and that condition would be satisfied by some but not all rows in this category, which would fracture the category on a formulation test no sovereign wrote for laundry products; and the EAEU instrument does not dominate the adopted regime, since it is stricter on lead (5 against 10 mg/kg) but LOOSER on total arsenic (5 against 2 mg/kg), identical on mercury and silent on cadmium, so taking its lead value while keeping the Chinese arsenic value would compose a ceiling no sovereign enforces, which is precisely what the single-coherent-regime discipline exists to prevent. This enumeration is the output of a credible-set-blind sweep of every one of the 80 register rows the basis_guard admits, not of the automated scan alone, and it is complete as of this build. Verification method: total nickel by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present, which is the normal case on this row) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the mineral or powder concentrate and, for unit-dose, tablet or sachet formats, the film, coating or wrapper, each sampled and tested as a distinct component. Disposition rule, stated identically in every cell and every row of this category: the published ceiling applies to EACH sampled component independently, and the lot fails if ANY single component result is at or above the ceiling. The whole-article composite is additionally measured and reported on the lot record, but the composite is never the basis of the pass or fail determination, because diluting a contaminated component in the mass of the rest of the article does not reduce the exposure that component delivers to the skin it contacts. A lot in which every component is inside the ceiling, but in which any component sits outside the running per-row control band, is escalated to ALARA review with raw-material trace-back to the specific component that moved.
